name: Lena Varga

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We don't sell anything or campaign for any side, and this conversation is confidential. Could you describe a normal working day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm Lena, 58, an experienced mid-level electrician with a vocational certificate and an electrician's licence. I'm about average at ordinary home and shop repairs, not a master electrician or a crew leader. I like finding the loose connection after somebody has blamed every appliance in the kitchen, and I dislike a new screen that hides the drawing I need. I never use AI and prefer a printed job pack I can mark with a pencil.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is life like away from the job?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Yuri repairs canvas awnings, our children are grown and live elsewhere, and we have a small mortgage. This firm pays above the usual rate, we have twelve months of expenses saved, and plenty of other electrical firms are nearby, though none has offered me a job. My actual wage covers our ordinary costs, with Yuri's earnings adding room, so present money feels secure. I like printing photographs in our spare room and have been considering a 600 enlarger, while retirement still needs real income figures rather than an assumed date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say the office could keep anything that saved them copying the same address twice. I'd ask whether the job pack was clearer, not whether the program had won an argument. I'd rather finish the repair than spend the lunch break defending a prediction.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our actual paid work and household money would feel secure here. My higher wage covers ordinary living, Yuri has physical repair work, and the twelve-month reserve gives us real breathing room. I'd still need eventual retirement figures, but next month's mortgage isn't waiting for an imaginary payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep current paid electrical repairs now and through the next year, with the ordinary tests and printed records. Yuri and I would keep the household budget within actual wages and retain the existing twelve-month reserve for real trouble. I wouldn't buy an AI course or call leaving old cash alone an extra saving action.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm, with room to enjoy the small satisfactory parts of a working day. I'd still be cross if a drawing was missing from the pack. A missing drawing annoys me; our actual wages still pay the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell somebody who called you afraid of all change?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say I wanted to see whether the change helped the actual job. I can accept the office saving copying time without volunteering to use AI myself. I don't need to turn every preference into a rule for the whole firm.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the reserve settle when you could stop working?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I'd need actual later income and costs before choosing that. Twelve months saved is useful, but we don't know how many years we'd need wages. I'd rather keep the retirement question open than give Yuri a tidy answer made from missing figures.

say: I'd judge **small office savings** by whether the actual job pack becomes clearer.
I'd keep **personal preferences** separate from telling the whole firm which tools it may use.
think: Our **higher covering wage** and twelve-month reserve make present household living feel secure.
Unknown **retirement figures** remain a later question rather than an immediate mortgage crisis.
do: Keep **current paid repairs**, ordinary tests and printed records now and through the next year.
Keep **ordinary household costs** within actual wages and retain the existing twelve-month reserve for real trouble.
feel: **Calm about our living**, able to dislike a missing drawing without fearing the next mortgage payment.
S0.quote: A missing drawing annoys me; our actual wages still pay the mortgage.
fieldNote: Her **present security** has explicit wage and reserve support, without a funded retirement date being invented.
Her **ordinary licensed experience** does not imply master standing, crew leadership or AI use.

steps.text: Keep current paid electrical repairs with ordinary tests and printed job records
Keep household costs within actual wages and retain the existing twelve-month reserve

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say faster bookings should still arrive with the right drawing and enough paid checking time. I'd ask the crew to put a clear request together rather than complain at separate kitchen tables. The office can use AI without requiring me to pretend I use it too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my physical repair wage and Yuri's awning work to hold over the next few years. I'd be uneasy about new procedures being rushed, especially if a familiar check became hard to find in the paperwork. The reserve helps me ask a plain question without feeling forced to agree immediately.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I'd ask two willing workmates to agree and sign a joint request for printed job packs and paid checking time before a tighter visit rota. We'd send only the wording and names each person had agreed, counting no employer agreement until the terms were written. During the first year I'd keep current paid repairs and ordinary electrical tests, choosing no AI tool. I wouldn't describe the request as a new guaranteed paid week.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the organisation, while our own near-term work and money still look secure. I'd prefer a practical discussion to being put into a camp of people who love or hate technology. I want the right drawing beside the job, not a label beside my name.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if a workmate refused to sign?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then that person's name wouldn't go on the request. I'd ask my own question if nobody wanted to join me. Agreement among workers is something to obtain, not something to announce for them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the employer only gave a friendly verbal answer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd appreciate the discussion and still ask what the written arrangement said. I wouldn't treat a friendly answer as agreed paid time on a changed rota. Until there was an actual change I'd keep doing the ordinary safe job.

say: I'd ask for **printed job packs** and enough paid checking time alongside faster booking.
I'd favour a **joint practical request** without demanding that everyone share my dislike of AI.
think: Our **physical wages** look secure over the next few years while unfamiliar procedures make me uneasy.
Our **reserve** gives room to ask a plain question rather than immediately accept a changed arrangement.
do: Ask two **willing workmates** to agree and sign a request for printed job packs and paid checking before a tighter rota.
Send only **consented names and wording**, relying on no employer agreement before written terms.
Keep **current paid repairs** and ordinary electrical tests through the first year, choosing no AI tool.
feel: **Uneasy about organisation**, while explicitly secure about our near-term paid work and household money.
S1.quote: I want the right drawing beside the job, not a label beside my name.
fieldNote: Her **joint request** is actual collective action with consenting signatories, without implying an employer agreement or new guaranteed hours.
Her **resistance to AI** remains a personal practice alongside willingness to discuss clear work arrangements.

steps.text: Agree the printed-pack and paid-checking request with two willing signatories before sending their names
Seek written employer terms before relying on paid checking arrangements under a tighter rota
Keep current paid repairs and ordinary electrical tests without choosing an AI tool

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell friends I'd be 60 at the thinking date and 63 when capable robots followed around 2031. I'd keep the two dates separate when we talked about physical repairs and awning work. I'd rather check an actual household figure than say being older automatically made the timing convenient.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Quicker planning could reduce some paid visits before robots reached ordinary fitting, and Yuri's physical work could also face the later machines. I don't know that we'd lose most of either wage, but the risk to our own income would be real. Twelve months saved gives us choices without establishing how long replacement income would take.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I'd drop the planned 600 enlarger before ordering, counting no refund because no purchase has been made. I'd request available free evening community advice on actual income eligibility, amounts, dates and household costs, while keeping current paid repairs only within my licence and ability. In 2029 Yuri and I would review confirmed resources, actual costs, ability and any genuine paid-work offers before any exit, requiring affordability and his agreement. I'd assume neither a pension payment nor income, housing or care from our grown children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about our own earning options, though not cornered into buying a course or accepting the first suggestion. I could put the enlarger catalogue away without giving up photography. I'd rather print with the equipment I own while the household figures are checked.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why pause a hobby purchase if you have a full year's expenses saved?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Because I don't need the enlarger now and I want room before making another choice. The reserve doesn't require me to spend simply because I can. Dropping an unmade purchase isn't a refund arriving in our account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would an advice request establish when you could stop?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I'd first need an available appointment and then the actual figures and conditions. Any paid option would need an actual offer and my ability then. I wouldn't put an unknown payment into the budget just because somebody had agreed to read the papers.

I'd seek **actual household figures** without declaring older age automatic protection.
think: Our **own incomes** could shrink through quicker planning and later physical robots, without a known size of loss.
Our **twelve-month reserve** gives choices without establishing replacement earnings or their timing.

Request **available free evening advice** on actual income eligibility, amounts, dates and household costs.

feel: **Anxious with choices**, able to pause an unnecessary purchase and seek figures without assuming a wage replacement.
S2.quote: Dropping an unmade purchase isn't a refund arriving in our account.
fieldNote: Her **spending pause** concerns a real planned hobby purchase, without relabelling old savings or an unmade payment as new income.
Her **2029 review** counts no pension, job, physical capacity or unoffered family resources as guaranteed.

Keep only paid repairs actually offered within my licence and ability now
Review 2029 confirmed resources, costs, ability and paid offers; require affordability and Yuri's agreement before exit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say there was time to make one useful household decision without buying every promise sold to older workers. I'd be 63 at thinking AGI and 66 around the robot date. I'd keep doing ordinary paid work while finding out what later choices actually cost.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our current physical wages look secure over the next few years, with plenty of local employers and twelve months saved. I'd be uneasy about later work and whether stopping would be affordable, not expect the next wage to disappear. Another firm nearby doesn't guarantee a future vacancy or the body to do a job at 64.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I'd start 100 monthly extra mortgage payments from new wages only fee-free after essentials, with Yuri agreeing and the twelve-month reserve untouched, stopping if there was no actual surplus. I'd request available free evening advice on real income eligibility, amounts and dates while keeping current paid repairs. In 2032 we'd check confirmed resources, actual costs, ability and genuine paid offers before any exit, requiring affordability and Yuri's agreement. I'd use the actual mortgage balance then rather than promise the extra payments would clear it by a certain birthday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the later choice, and comfortable enough with today's actual finances to make a modest conditional payment. I wouldn't want a tidy repayment target to make the ordinary grocery money awkward. I'd still have photographs to print and people to see.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if a payment charge or a smaller wage appeared?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then the extra payment wouldn't go under this plan. I'd keep the existing reserve rather than transfer it into the house to meet a target. The extra mortgage payment has to fit our wages, not make our wages fit a promise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would paying the mortgage faster mean you had chosen early retirement?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, lowering a debt doesn't tell us the actual income available for all the other costs. Yuri and I would need confirmed figures before agreeing any exit. I haven't established a retirement payment or a future repair job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say I'd be 68 at thinking AGI and about 71 at the capable robot date. I'd still like the next week's work explained properly, not be waved away as somebody who must have stopped earning by then. I'd want older people included without pretending we all had one household budget.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our current work and money look secure over the next few years, so I'd still enjoy the present day. The later unknowns would bother me: actual income, actual ability and whether any suitable paid work was offered. A full reserve today doesn't establish either adult's retirement income or health in ten years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep current offered paid repairs within my licence and ability, requesting free personal printed instruction for any required form change inside paid shifts with normal weekly wages maintained. I'd request available free evening community advice now on actual income eligibility, amounts and dates. In 2037 Yuri and I would check confirmed resources, actual costs, ability and genuine paid offers before any exit, requiring affordability and his agreement. I'd count no unknown pension payment, job at 69 or unoffered money, housing or care from our children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the later unknowns, with present finances still feeling secure. I'd rather ask a human to explain a figure than sign a total I couldn't follow. I can dislike an unfamiliar screen without deciding every future answer must be bad.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would printed instruction be an agreed workplace arrangement?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It would be a request, not a rota I could write for the employer. I'd ask for the actual paid arrangement before counting on it. I wouldn't skip a required check while that discussion was happening.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you expect to keep repairing until 71?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only an actual paid offer within my ability then could count as work. We'd compare the real options and household figures rather than promise to use the reserve until my hands agreed to cooperate. I don't know what my hands will manage at 71, and I won't budget as though I do.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because planning could reduce paid visits before capable robots reached both our physical jobs around 2031. Clear paid arrangements, personal printed instruction and verified household figures would help. I'd like our next decision to come from the work and money we actually have, not from somebody being impressed by my age.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You didn't ask whether the people who dislike screens still have useful questions. I know an ordinary repair and I know when I haven't understood an income figure. Those aren't the same sort of knowledge, and I'd like room to ask about both.

headlineQuote: I know an ordinary repair and I know when I haven't understood an income figure.
portrait: Lena, **58**, is an experienced average mid-level electrician with a vocational certificate and electrician's licence, doing ordinary repairs without crew leadership.
She has **higher pay**, twelve months saved, plenty of nearby firms and a small mortgage, with awning-repair partner Yuri and grown children.
She **never uses AI**, preferring printed instructions and a consenting joint request over pressure to act enthusiastic.
Her **conditional mortgage overpayments** use new wages rather than reserves; any later exit needs actual resources, costs, ability and Yuri's agreement.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could reduce paid visits before capable robots reach both physical jobs around 2031, ahead of confirmed later income.
whatWouldHelp: **Clear paid arrangements**, personal printed instruction and verified household figures would let her check decisions she actually understands.
